title: Air India to Launch Non-Stop Delhi-Osaka Flights From February 2, 2027
excerpt: Four weekly Boeing 787-8 services will make Osaka Air India's second Japan destination, with open-jaw Tokyo options for Golden Route travellers.
body:
• Air India will start non-stop Delhi to Osaka (Kansai) flights on 2 February 2027, four times a week on Boeing 787-8 aircraft.
  • Flight AI360 leaves Delhi at 22:50 on Tuesdays, Thursdays, Saturdays and Sundays, arriving Osaka at 09:50 next morning; AI359 returns at 11:50, arriving Delhi at 18:20.
  • Osaka becomes Air India's second Japan destination after Tokyo Haneda, and the airline will be the only carrier non-stop on Delhi-Osaka.
  • Reader utility: bookings are opening progressively on Air India's website and app — travellers can book open-jaw trips, into Osaka and out of Tokyo, for Golden Route itineraries covering Tokyo, Kyoto and Osaka.

Air India will launch non-stop flights between Delhi and Osaka from 2 February 2027, adding a second Japanese city to its network as Indian travel to Japan continues to climb sharply. The airline said it will be the only carrier operating non-stop on the Delhi-Osaka route.

According to Air India's official announcement, the service will run four times a week using Boeing 787-8 aircraft configured with 18 full-flat beds in business class and 241 seats in economy class. Osaka, served through Kansai International Airport, is Japan's second-largest metropolitan area.

Schedule designed for connections

Travel Trade Journal's coverage of the schedule lists AI360 departing Delhi at 22:50 on Tuesdays, Thursdays, Saturdays and Sundays and arriving in Osaka at 09:50 the following morning, local times. The return, AI359, departs Osaka at 11:50 on Mondays, Wednesdays, Fridays and Sundays and arrives in Delhi at 18:20 the same day.

"Osaka, served through Kansai International Airport, is Japan's second-largest metropolitan area."

The late-evening departure from Delhi and late-morning return from Osaka are timed, the airline said, to offer onward connections across its domestic and international network through Delhi. For travellers starting in other Indian cities, that means a single connection in Delhi rather than a stop in a third country, which has until now been the usual route to Kansai.

Building on Tokyo

Osaka joins Tokyo Haneda, where Air India currently operates daily flights from Delhi and four weekly flights from Mumbai. The expansion reflects sustained demand rather than a one-off seasonal addition: the new route is scheduled as a regular four-weekly service from its February start.

The airline also highlighted open-jaw flexibility. Travellers can fly into Osaka and return from Tokyo, or the other way round, without backtracking. That matters for the itinerary most first-time Indian visitors follow — the so-called Golden Route linking Tokyo, Kyoto and Osaka — where backtracking to a single arrival airport wastes a day.

Why demand is rising

Japan welcomed more than 315,000 Indian visitors in 2025, according to the Japan National Tourism Organization figures cited by Air India. That was a 35 percent increase over 2024 and nearly 80 percent above pre-pandemic levels. Air India attributed the growth to interest in leisure, cultural and culinary experiences, alongside expanding business and people-to-people ties.

For the Indian diaspora, the route is useful in two ways. Families in India planning Japan holidays gain a direct option into Kansai, close to Kyoto and Nara as well as Osaka itself. Diaspora travellers combining a trip home with a Japan stop can also build Delhi into the routing, using the airline's network rather than separate tickets through other hubs — though travellers should check baggage and connection protections when booking separate tickets.

What to check before booking

Bookings are being made available progressively through Air India's official website, mobile app, contact centre, airport ticketing offices and travel agents. Travellers should confirm the operating days for their specific dates, as the outbound and return flights operate on different weekdays, and check Japan visa requirements well ahead of a February departure.

The February 2027 start also gives travellers planning spring trips — including cherry-blossom season itineraries that typically run from late March — a new direct entry point into western Japan. Whether Air India adds frequency will likely depend on how quickly the four-weekly service fills, but the route establishes a direct Delhi-Kansai link that did not previously exist.
